description: Indulge in a restaurant-quality New York Strip Steak right at home, perfectly seared and basted with rich garlic herb butter. This iconic American dish promises a tender, juicy interior and a beautifully caramelized crust, making it an ideal centerpiece for any special dinner. Experience the ultimate steakhouse flavor in your own kitchen with this easy-to-follow recipe.

ingredients.notes: high smoke point oil like avocado oil also works
1 stick, cold and cut into cubes

instructions.title: Prepare the Steaks
instructions.text: Remove steaks from the refrigerator 30-60 minutes before cooking to bring them closer to room temperature. Pat them very dry with paper towels. Season generously all over with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper. This step is crucial for a good crust.

instructions.title: Heat the Skillet
instructions.text: Heat a heavy-bottomed skillet, preferably cast iron, over high heat until smoking lightly. Add the olive oil to the hot pan and swirl to coat the bottom.

instructions.title: Sear the Steaks
instructions.text: Carefully place the seasoned steaks into the hot skillet. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side for a medium-rare to medium internal temperature, developing a deep brown crust. Adjust cooking time based on steak thickness and desired doneness.

instructions.title: Add Garlic Butter and Herbs
instructions.text: Reduce the heat to medium. Add the cold cubed butter, smashed garlic cloves, and fresh rosemary or thyme sprigs to the skillet. The butter should melt and foam. Tilt the pan slightly to pool the butter.

instructions.title: Baste the Steaks
instructions.text: Using a large spoon, continuously baste the melted garlic herb butter over the steaks for 1-2 minutes, ensuring all surfaces are coated. This infuses the steaks with incredible flavor and helps create an even crust.

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the steaks from the skillet and transfer them to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil and let them rest for at least 5-10 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, resulting in a more tender and juicy steak. Slice against the grain and garnish with fresh parsley, if desired, before serving.

tags: New York Strip Steak Garlic Butter
tips: Always pat your steaks very dry before seasoning and searing. Excess moisture prevents a proper crust from forming.
Use a meat thermometer to ensure desired doneness: 130-135F for medium-rare, 135-140F for medium. Remember the temperature will rise a few degrees while resting.
Do not skip the resting step! It is critical for a juicy steak. Cutting too soon will cause all the delicious juices to run out.
